rv.q: This is a group moving perfectly in concert, as elegantly balanced as dancers.
The all-male casting brings depth and subtlety of meaning, proving ingenious rather than gimmicky, simultaneously nostalgic and of the moment.
This is a subtle and lively version of one of Shakespeare's greatest comedies, full of light, laughter and love.
This fresh, gently moving production, packed with wonderful performances and keenly observant about the universal need for love and acceptance.
Somewhat laboured comedy enlivened by a warm, all-male cast
The same sophistication eludes Daniel Evans’s stylish and fun but curiously insubstantial revival.

More than an hour passed before the actors returned to the stage, cheered on by an audience that was clearly anxious to see more of Jonathan Groff’s winningly vulnerable Rosalind. This was, remarkably enough, the American star’s Shakespearean debut.
The result is a work of genius, sublime from start to finish and sparkling with joy.
This production of As It is bold, joyful, crowd-pleasing stuff, addressing timeless human emotions in a thoroughly modern but authentically Shakespearean way.
More than anything though, this is just a wonderfully whimsical, splendidly upbeat production that delighted, amused and roused us into a frenzy.
Daniel Evans' new RSC production is something else, though - one to turn even AYLI sceptics into devotees.
They did likewise with a standing ovation at the conclusion of this thoroughly interesting and idiosyncratic production of As It.
This is an extremely enjoyable As It, and one of the clearest Shakespeare productions I have seen in some time.

cn.t: The RSC's all-male "As You Like It" delights critics with Jonathan Groff's charismatic Rosalind leading an exceptional ensemble through Shakespeare's comedy with wit, warmth, and clarity under Daniel Evans' inventive direction.
